question: Why does the household installation save so often and write so much per save?
installation: Household installation, Raspberry Pi 5, Home Assistant 2026.10.0, Homeostatic 1.9.0, about 6,000 entities and 300 devices; store file .storage/homeostatic.<entry>
method: Two copies of the store file taken 60 seconds apart during an idle minute, sized per section as compact JSON and compared field by field; save causes from the coalesced saves receipt's idle window. Aggregates only; no household data is recorded here.

file.note: Home Assistant's Store writes two-space indented JSON; the indentation is 2.3 MB of the 7.7 MB.

attention_routes.note: Each route signature stores the full JSON of the same 13 rules; a digest would compare equally.

changes_between_two_idle_saves_one_minut.check_evidence: current.observed_at changed in all 1,675 records (0.28 MB); last_failure in 36
changes_between_two_idle_saves_one_minut.engine: checks changed (1.48 MB): each check record carries its last observation with its time
changes_between_two_idle_saves_one_minut.unchanged: enrollment, episodes, resolved_history, operator_controls, delivery, attention_routes and the other 14 sections

why_every_minute_saves: The minute reconcile re-observes every check and records the observation time in the evidence and engine sections, so the snapshot differs every minute even when no condition changed; the coalescing window then writes it once.
write_volume_estimate: 7.7 MB per save at 1.55 saves a minute is about 17 GB a day on this installation; before 1.9.0 it was 2.5 to 2.8 saves a minute, about 30 GB a day
memory: Not measured: the Supervisor core stats endpoint refused the frontend session and the agent API does not expose it
open_question: Which engine events make a config-entry rewrite by another integration an immediate save; a per-refresh trace of event types answers it
